answer: During a voyage to map karst caves and pearl beds, surveying agents earn only for readings signed by certified sensor chips. A registry audits that each chip is enrolled once; every signature covers the epoch, location and fresh challenge. Validators reject a second claim for the same chip and epoch across all agent keys. Creating aliases cannot multiply a chip allowance. To obtain n allowances, an attacker must buy and deploy n certified devices, paying hardware and field costs; security depends on the registry preventing duplicate enrollment.
